The 2016 year of account deterioration during 2017 is due to fall back exposure to the hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2017 gross claims outstanding were GBP 350.266m. Analysis of the claims development triangle indicates negligible aggregate gross prior-year development for underwriting years up to 2015 (net prior-year development computed as effectively flat). The calendar-year movement reported a modest net favourable outcome (GBP 2.9m net) driven by lower-than-expected incurred movements across several long-tail casualty lines (notably reduced assessments on medical malpractice) and other favorable development; however reinsurance-to-close transactions and reinsurance recoveries are present in the accounts and can distort comparisons. The syndicate retains material catastrophe exposures (including the 2017 hurricanes and historical events such as Superstorm Sandy and 2010/11 international cat events) which were highlighted but not fully separated into gross prior-year reserve movements.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Gross prior-year development was derived from the published gross claims development triangle (claims note). The accounts also report net prior-year movements (a net surplus of GBP 2.9m) which differ from the gross triangle result; reinsurance-to-close (RITC) activity (acceptance of RITC from Syndicate 6103) and funds-withheld arrangements are present and can distort comparisons between gross and net movements. Where the report provided only net figures, these were not used for the gross PYD. Gross PYD computed as zero from the triangle; confidence lowered because RITC and inter-syndicate arrangements may mask some gross movements.
